what_happened: The person running Athena re-asked the slowest-tests job (20261102-001711-pgvq) with a request that had the producer read test timings from GitHub's CI logs. The producer works in a sealed snapshot with no GitHub access, so it could not get the data. It gave up within seconds and the job failed with nothing produced. The person running Athena then logged this as their own mistake.
cause: Neither the request writer nor Athena is shown what the producer can reach, and nothing compares a request's data sources against that list before dispatch. Requests are written from what the person running Athena can see (GitHub, CI logs), not from what the sealed snapshot holds. Like other design-from-assumption mistakes, the gap shows up only when the job fails.
prevention: Add an admission check that scans a request and its reading for data sources outside the producer's snapshot (CI logs, GitHub API, other branches, network). It should refuse the job, or have Athena fetch the data into a file in the snapshot before dispatch. Also give request writers the list of what the producer can and cannot see. This covers the whole class, not only CI logs.
proposed_request: Make Athena check, before a job is dispatched, that every data source its request and accepted reading depend on is reachable from the producer's sealed snapshot. Outcome: if a request needs CI logs, GitHub data or other outside data, Athena either fetches it before dispatch and places it in the snapshot as a file the producer can read, or refuses the job at admission with a message naming the unreachable source. Then re-queue the slowest-tests job (20261102-001711-pgvq) so Athena supplies the test timings from the latest CI run as a file in the snapshot, and the producer measures the slowest tests and fixes the biggest cause. Acceptance: (1) a test shows a request naming CI logs is either given the fetched file or refused with a clear reason; (2) the producer prompt or brief states what it can and cannot see; (3) the re-queued job's entry holds real measured timings or a stated reason.
